Cc: 
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: pricing for pilot — who signs & who pays?

Hi Ava / Daniel —

Great to meet earlier — quick written recap and a couple of asks so we can keep procurement moving.

Recap (from today’s discovery):
- Pilot scope: 3-week canary using the Redwood hosted endpoint for 5k concurrent users (expected bursty traffic), sample dataset for de-identification flow.
- Expected volume: rough estimate 30M–50M tokens/month in pilot window; if pilot converts, projected steady-state 200M tokens/month.
- Primary success metric: latency ≤ 250ms p50 for single-turn gen and acceptable quality on the eval prompt set.

Open questions / asks (could you confirm these?):
1) Who is the economic buyer that signs the final PO/SOW? (name & email)
2) Who owns payment/finance approval (AP contact or procurement alias)?
3) Target $/1M tokens you’re budgeting for (range is fine) — we usually push a few pricing options depending on committed volume.
4) Any procurement constraints/timelines (e.g., required PO, net terms, security paperwork deadline).

Attached: Redwood_Pilot_Estimate_v1.pdf (high-level cost scenarios) and SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf. The estimate includes per-1M token unit costs at three tier volumes.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm economic buyer + finance contact so I can list them on the SOW.
- If ok, I’ll ask our finance team to prepare a formal quote and SOW (DocuSign link + invoice terms).

If it helps, we can also sketch a constrained pilot pricing with a one-month refundable credit to lower initial risk.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | (415) 555-0126

---
Attachment stubs:
- Redwood_Pilot_Estimate_v1.pdf (15 KB)
- SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf (340 KB)

From: Ava Roberts <ava.roberts@finexa.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@finexa.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: pricing for pilot — who signs & who pays?

Thanks Kimberly — good summary and helpful attachments. Quick answers below:

1) Economic buyer: Daniel Cho (VP, Platform) — daniel.cho@finexa.com (copied on this thread). He’ll sign the SOW for pilot and any renewal.
2) Finance/procurement contact: procure@finexa.com — they handle PO issuance and invoices.
3) Budget target: For initial commercial discussions, our internal guidance is in the range of $60k–$120k/month (target $/1M tokens we’re thinking closer to $70–$80 per 1M for a multi-month committed deal), but that’s flexible based on performance and SLA.
4) Timeline: Procurement needs a SOW + cost breakdown to raise a PO; they typically require a 2–3 week review cycle. Net30 is standard.

A couple of clarifying Qs from our side:
- Can you share the per-1M token rows explicitly in the quote (pilot tier, mid-tier, enterprise committed)?
- Is there an option for a short trial credit or a capped spend for the pilot?

Looping in procurement by copying procure@finexa.com. If you want, we can set a 30-min call with Daniel next week to align on sign-off timelines.

Best,
Ava Roberts
Head of Product Partnerships | Finexa Health
ava.roberts@finexa.com

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. I’m the signatory for the pilot — happy to move forward provided procurement has the SOW + unitized quote. A few notes from finance/procurement side:

- Procurement contact is procure@finexa.com (copied). They require a vendor W-9 and a single-line invoice or DocuSign SOW to generate a PO.
- Standard terms: Net30; we prefer consolidated monthly invoices.
- For the pilot we’re comfortable with a capped spend approach (please call out the credit in the SOW); Daniel prefers a $10k capped trial credit for the pilot stage.

Could you send a one-page quote that explicitly shows the $/1M token rows by tier and the pilot credit applied? If you can include a DocuSign-ready SOW that we can sign electronically, procurement can usually produce a PO within 10 business days.

Happy to do a 30-min alignment call Tues or Wed — Ava and I can make time.
